_doc: Per-page metadata for the Category-24 (Dairy and Milk Products) standard renderer (tools/build-category-standard-pages.mjs). Numbers come from data/standards/cat24-compiled/<record>.json — frozen copies of the index repo's deterministic government-limit compiler (tools/standards/compile-cat24.mjs); no values are authored here. This file carries display + wiring + the category _meta block only.

_meta.tier_footnote: Inorganic arsenic (iAs) and hexavalent chromium (Cr-VI) operate as reflex speciation screens — total arsenic and total chromium are measured on every lot and bound them. Methylmercury (MeHg) has no bioaccumulation pathway in dairy and is bounded by total mercury. Tin (Sn) is material only for canned product (condensed and evaporated milks), where it migrates from the can; for all other dairy forms it is controlled by screen, not assigned an invented number. Nickel and aluminium carry disclosed read-across limits where no government sets a general-dairy maximum. Dairy has no legislated reconstitution ratio, so every limit is taken at face value in the product's native basis.
_meta.methodology_version: Method v2.0 — government-limit default (CLAUDE.md Part 19, Governing Principles v2.0)
_meta.manual_method_note: Dairy limits are taken at face value in each product's native basis; there is no reconstitution conversion (dairy has no legislated reconstitution ratio, unlike infant formula). Product forms — liquid milk, cheese, powder, condensed, butterfat — are kept distinct: non-concentrated liquid forms share the general fluid-milk sovereign pool, while concentrated forms carry their own higher form-specific government maximums. Tier 1 toxics (Pb, Cd, iAs, Hg) are zero-tolerance; Tier 2 (tAs, Ni, Sn, Al, Cr, Cr-VI) are held to the same government limit; tiering sets the reaction to an exceedance, not any permission to exceed it. Inorganic arsenic and hexavalent chromium are reflex speciation screens; methylmercury has no pathway in dairy; tin is material only for canned product.

pages.name: Liquid milk — cow
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for liquid cow's milk — raw, pasteurized, and UHT fluid milk — stated as consumed. Every numeric limit is the strictest maximum level any credible government sets for fluid milk; where no government regulates the exact analyte, a disclosed read-across from the nearest sovereign value applies.

pages.name: Liquid milk — goat, sheep, and other ruminant
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for goat, sheep, and other ruminant fluid milk, stated as consumed. Sovereign fluid-milk contaminant maximums are species-agnostic, so this standard shares the general fluid-milk pool with cow's milk; every limit is the strictest government maximum, with a disclosed read-across where none regulates the exact analyte.

pages.name: Camel milk
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified standard for camel milk sold as a general beverage, stated as consumed. No government sets camel-milk-specific maximums, so the species-agnostic fluid-milk sovereign limits apply as a disclosed same-matrix government limit; camel-milk infant formula is out of scope and routes to the infant-foods standard.
